```plato

    // The von Mises CDF of the WRAPPED angle, with the cut at the antipode:
    // F(mu - pi) = 0 and F -> 1 as value -> mu + pi, and any real input is
    // first wrapped into [mu - pi, mu + pi). There is NO closed form; this is
    // the standard Fourier/Bessel series (Abramowitz & Stegun 9.6.34 applied
    // to the density),
    //     F(x) = 1/2 + (x-mu)/(2 pi)
    //          + (1/(pi I0(kappa))) * sum_j I_j(kappa) sin(j (x-mu)) / j,
    // truncated at 32 terms. The terms decay like exp(-j^2/(2 kappa)), so for
    // Concentration <= 15 (the full-accuracy regime of the Bessel kernel) the
    // truncation error is below ~1e-10 absolute; accuracy degrades gradually
    // beyond that. At kappa = 0 the series vanishes exactly (I_j(0) = 0),
    // leaving the circular uniform CDF 1/2 + (x-mu)/(2 pi).
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Von_Mises_distribution
    Cdf(self: VonMisesDistribution, value: Number): Number
    {
        var x = value - self.MeanDirection.Radians;
        var wrapped = x - Number.Tau * ((x + Number.Pi) / Number.Tau).Floor;
        var uniformPart = 0.5 + wrapped / Number.Tau;
        return self.Concentration <= 0.0
            ? uniformPart
            : uniformPart
              + SumOf(32.MapRange(j =>
                    VonMisesBesselI(j + 1, self.Concentration)
                    * Angle((j.ToNumber + 1.0) * wrapped).Sin
                    / (j.ToNumber + 1.0)))
                / (Number.Pi * BesselI0(self.Concentration));
    }

    //==
    // # Discrete distribution bodies
    //
    // The `IProbabilityDistribution` obligations for the types of
    // `random.types.plato`. Pdf reads the probability mass at the value rounded
    // down to a whole number, per that file's convention. The Binomial and Poisson
    // CDFs sum the masses directly — exact in form and O(k) — because their closed
    // forms are regularized incomplete beta and gamma functions, which this tree
    // cannot express. Factorial and BinomialCoefficient come from the shared
    // helpers at the top of this library.

    //==
    // # BernoulliDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: SuccessProbability (p) in [0, 1]. Support is {0, 1};
    // per the section note above, Pdf reads the mass at the value rounded down.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernoulli_distribution

    // The mean: the success probability.
    Mean(self: BernoulliDistribution): Number
        => self.SuccessProbability.Value;

    // The variance: p * (1 - p).
    Variance(self: BernoulliDistribution): Number
        => self.SuccessProbability.Value * (1.0 - self.SuccessProbability.Value);

    // The mass at floor(value): p at 1, 1 - p at 0, zero elsewhere. Exact.
    Pdf(self: BernoulliDistribution, value: Number): Number
        => value.Floor == 1.0
            ? self.SuccessProbability.Value
            : value.Floor == 0.0
                ? 1.0 - self.SuccessProbability.Value
                : 0.0;

    // The step CDF: 0 below zero, 1 - p on [0, 1), 1 at or above one. Exact.
    Cdf(self: BernoulliDistribution, value: Number): Number
        => value < 0.0
            ? 0.0
            : value < 1.0
                ? 1.0 - self.SuccessProbability.Value
                : 1.0;

    //==
    // # BinomialDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: TrialCount (n) independent trials each succeeding with
    // SuccessProbability (p). Support is the whole numbers 0..n; Pdf reads the
    // mass at the value rounded down. Precondition: TrialCount >= 0.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binomial_distribution

    // The mean: n * p.
    Mean(self: BinomialDistribution): Number
        => self.TrialCount.ToNumber * self.SuccessProbability.Value;

    // The variance: n * p * (1 - p).
    Variance(self: BinomialDistribution): Number
        => self.TrialCount.ToNumber * self.SuccessProbability.Value
         * (1.0 - self.SuccessProbability.Value);

    // The mass at k = floor(value): C(n, k) * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k) inside the
    // support, zero outside. Exact in form; the coefficient is built by the
    // multiplicative recurrence, so large n loses precision but does not
    // overflow through an intermediate factorial.
    Pdf(self: BinomialDistribution, value: Number): Number
    {
        var k = value.Floor.ToInteger;
        var p = self.SuccessProbability.Value;
        return k < 0 || k > self.TrialCount
            ? 0.0
            : BinomialCoefficient(self.TrialCount, k)
                * p.Pow(k.ToNumber)
                * (1.0 - p).Pow((self.TrialCount - k).ToNumber);
    }

    // The cumulative mass at k = floor(value), by direct summation of the masses
    // 0..k. Exact in form and O(k); the closed form is a regularized incomplete
    // beta, which this tree cannot express.
    Cdf(self: BinomialDistribution, value: Number): Number
    {
        var k = value.Floor.ToInteger;
        return k < 0
            ? 0.0
            : k >= self.TrialCount
                ? 1.0
                : (k + 1).Range
                    .Map(i => self.Pdf(i.ToNumber))
                    .Reduce(0.0, (total, mass) => total + mass);
    }

    //==
    // # GeometricDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: the number of FAILURES BEFORE the first success, so the
    // support is {0, 1, 2, ...} — NOT the "number of trials" variant supported
    // on {1, 2, ...}, which has mean 1/p. This matches the type's doc comment.
    // Precondition: SuccessProbability > 0.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geometric_distribution

    // The mean number of failures before the first success: (1 - p) / p.
    Mean(self: GeometricDistribution): Number
        => (1.0 - self.SuccessProbability.Value) / self.SuccessProbability.Value;

    // The variance: (1 - p) / p^2.
    Variance(self: GeometricDistribution): Number
        => (1.0 - self.SuccessProbability.Value)
         / self.SuccessProbability.Value.Square;

    // The mass at k = floor(value): (1-p)^k * p for k >= 0, zero below. Exact.
    Pdf(self: GeometricDistribution, value: Number): Number
        => value < 0.0
            ? 0.0
            : (1.0 - self.SuccessProbability.Value).Pow(value.Floor)
                * self.SuccessProbability.Value;

    // The cumulative mass at k = floor(value): 1 - (1-p)^(k+1) for k >= 0, zero
    // below. Exact.
    Cdf(self: GeometricDistribution, value: Number): Number
        => value < 0.0
            ? 0.0
            : 1.0 - (1.0 - self.SuccessProbability.Value).Pow(value.Floor + 1.0);
```
